slides.notes:
Welcome learners as they arrive.
Point to the title and read it: "It happened so fast." Say: "Tonight we talk about a small car accident. No one is hurt. Only a dent."
Read the three lines under "Today you will". Give one quick example of each: "At 8:00 I was driving to work." • "I was waiting at the light when a car hit my car." • "Was anyone hurt? No, everyone was OK."
Keep it simple and non-graphic: this lesson is about dents, not injuries. Never ask about real accidents, injuries, or experiences with the police. Use the pictures and the invented stories. If a learner starts a personal story, thank them and go back to the picture. Say once, clearly: "In a real emergency, call 911."

slides.title: It Happened So Fast

runs.t: By the end of class, you can do these six things.
A small accident. No one is hurt.
I can say what I was doing.
At 8:00 I was driving to work.
I can ask Were you…? and Was anyone hurt?
I can tell what happened with when and while.
I can answer an insurance agent's questions.
I can say what people were doing in a picture.
I can read a story and fill out a report.

slides.notes:
Read each goal slowly. Learners repeat.
Goal 1: was / were + -ing (At 8:00 I was driving to work.). Goal 2: Were you…? → Yes, I was. / No, I wasn't. and Was anyone hurt? Goal 3: when and while (I was waiting at the light when a car hit my car.).
Goal 4: answer an insurance agent's questions about a small car accident. Goal 5: describe what people were doing in a picture (a witness). Goal 6: read a short accident story and fill out a simple accident report.
"We check at 7:25" = the Progress Check. It is not a test grade.
Lesson plan: At a glance: Objectives.

Listening script (the audio is coming soon; until then, read it aloud with a volunteer at a normal, friendly speed):
Narrator: Lesson four. Listening. Elena had a small car accident. Now she's calling her insurance company. Listen.
Mark: Safe Road Insurance, this is Mark. How can I help you?
Elena: Hi, this is Elena Ramos. I had a small car accident this morning.
Mark: I'm sorry to hear that. Was anyone hurt?
Elena: No, everyone was OK. But my car has a dent.
Mark: Where did it happen?
Elena: At the intersection of Oak Street and Second Avenue.
Mark: What were you doing when it happened?
Elena: I was driving to work. The light was red, so I stopped.
Mark: And what was the other driver doing?
Elena: He was talking on his phone. He wasn't looking, and he hit my car.
Mark: Did anyone see the accident?
Elena: Yes. Two people were crossing the street. One woman gave me her phone number.
Mark: Good. Did the police come?
Elena: Yes. A police officer came and wrote a report.
Mark: OK. Please send me the report number today.
Elena: I will. Thank you for your help.
Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

runs.t: I can say what I was doing at a time in the past.
I can tell what happened with when and while.
I can answer questions about a small car accident.
I can fill out a simple accident report.
A. Listen to the teacher. Circle a or b.
a. driving to work   b. waiting at the light
a. driving to work   b. waiting for the bus
a. Someone was hurt.   b. No one was hurt.
a. talking on the phone   b. crossing the street

slides.notes:
Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min. Individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
Part A: read each sentence slowly, 2 times. Learners circle a or b. Then click to show the answer (one click per item, 1 to 4).
Say: 1 "At eight o'clock this morning, I was driving to work." (a) • 2 "She was waiting for the bus when it started to rain." (b) • 3 "Was anyone hurt? No, everyone was OK." (b) • 4 "The other driver was talking on the phone." (a)
Parts B and C: learners do them alone. Walk around and help with the instructions only. B answers: 1 was, 2 were, 3 Were, 4 wasn't. C: answers will vary (for example I was cooking dinner when my friend called. / While I was walking to work, I saw an accident.).
Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "With a little help." 😐 "Not yet."
Scoring: A /4 + B /4 + C /2 = /10. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs more help hearing the past continuous (A), with was / were (B), and with when / while (C).
Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 5). If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 5 at 6:00, while learners arrive.
